descriptionChirho: To erect or construct a physical structure such as a house, temple, tower, vineyard wall, or synagogue. The wise man 'built his house on the rock' (Matt 7:24-26 okodomesen), a landowner 'built a tower' in his vineyard (Matt 21:33, Mark 12:1), and the centurion 'built us a synagogue' (Luke 7:5). Jesus prophesies rebuilding the temple in three days (Matt 26:61, Mark 14:58 oikodomeso). Other physical construction includes building tombs of the prophets (Matt 23:29, Luke 11:47-48), building barns (Luke 12:18), and the activity of building in Noah's day (Luke 17:28). Uniformly rendered arb 'bana' (build), deu 'baut/bauen', fra 'batir', heb 'bana' (build), hin 'banaya/banaunga' (built/will build), kor 'jieotda/seul' (built/erected), spa 'edifico/edificare'.

To strengthen, encourage, or build up a person, community, or the church in faith and spiritual maturity, used figuratively of spiritual growth and communal encouragement. The church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria was 'being built up' (Acts 9:31 oikodomoumene). Paul commends the Ephesian elders to the word of God's grace which is 'able to build you up' (Acts 20:32). Love 'builds up' (1 Cor 8:1 oikodomei), prophecy 'edifies the church' (1 Cor 14:4 oikodomei), and believers are 'being built up as a spiritual house' (1 Pet 2:5 oikodomeisthe). Rendered hin 'unnati karta hai' (promotes advancement), kor 'deog-eul seunda' (builds virtue), spa 'edifica' (edifies), preserving the metaphorical architecture-to-community transfer.

To build in a general sense that may encompass either literal construction or figurative edification depending on context, including rebuilding what was torn down and counting the cost before building. Jesus' mockers at the cross taunt 'the one building the temple' (Matt 27:40, Mark 15:29 oikodomon). The parable of counting the cost before building a tower (Luke 14:28-30 oikodomesai/oikodomein) uses construction as a wisdom metaphor. Paul warns 'if I build again what I tore down' (Gal 2:18 oikodomeo), blending literal and figurative registers. These occurrences resist clean classification into purely physical or purely spiritual senses.

One who builds; a builder or constructor, used substantively (as a participle functioning as a noun) of those engaged in building, especially of the builders who rejected the cornerstone in the Psalm 118:22 quotation. In Matt 21:42 and Mark 12:10 Jesus quotes 'the stone which the builders (oikodomountes) rejected has become the head of the corner'; likewise Luke 20:17, Acts 4:11 ('rejected by you the builders'), and 1 Pet 2:7. Rendered arb 'al-banna'un' (the builders/masons), heb 'bonim' (builders), hin 'rajmistriyon' (masons/bricklayers), kor 'geonchukjadeul' (construction workers), spa 'edificadores/constructores' (builders/constructors).
